title: Bounded finite-projective Hom comparison with any K-injective target
statement: Let C be a small site with topology J and commutative ring sheaf R. Let P be a bounded-above complex of R-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose every P^i is a retract of the finite free sheaf R^(r_i). Let M be bounded below, I a K-injective complex, and alpha:M→I a quasi-isomorphism. Then postcomposition by alpha in the internal Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pur-sheaf-hom] is a quasi-isomorphism. No lower bound on I is required [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

proof.text: Internal Hom from a finite free sheaf preserves short exact sequences. Precomposition with the splitting maps gives a retraction between the short Hom sequences. Apply the existing generic theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.shortExact_of_retract, now exposed in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.StrictlyPerfectDerivedInternalHom. Its unchanged proof uses stability of monomorphisms and epimorphisms under retracts and the induced retraction of homology onto zero; this is the retract calculation required here.

First take a quasi-isomorphism between bounded-below complexes M,N, with lower bounds aM,aN. For a fixed degree n put k=min(aM,aN)-n-1 and T=stupidTruncGE_k P. The terms of T are zero below k and isomorphic to the corresponding P terms above it. Thus T is bounded and each term still has exact internal Hom. Apply the bounded exact-term Hom comparison to T.

For each target M or N, precomposition along T→P is an isomorphism on Hom terms in degrees n-1,n,n+1. Below k the target Hom factor is zero; at and above k the source inclusion is invertible. The limit projection formula transports these factorwise isomorphisms to the product terms. They give a quasi-isomorphism in degree n. Naturality and two-out-of-three then transfer the bounded comparison for T to the comparison for P. Since n is arbitrary this proves the bounded-below comparison.

Module sheaves are Grothendieck and have enough injectives. Choose a bounded-below K-injective resolution T of M, using CochainComplex.KInjectiveResolution.exists_of_isStrictlyGE, whose proof applies Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.exists_quasiIso_injective. The preceding comparison applies to M→T. Let F,eta be the functorial K-injective resolution. Naturality for M→T and two-out-of-three show that Hom(P,eta_M) is a quasi-isomorphism: Hom(P,eta_T) and Hom(P,F(M→T)) are quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective targets. Naturality for alpha:M→I then proves Hom(P,alpha) is a quasi-isomorphism, using the same fact for eta_I and F(alpha).

theorem ringedSite_boundedFree_rhom_map_quasiIso
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (P : CochainComplex
      (ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hP : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (P.X i))
    (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ∃ s : P.X i ⟶ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)),
      ∃ t : SheafOfModules.free
        (R := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))
          ⟶ P.X i, s ≫ t = 𝟙 (P.X i))
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective]
    (M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hM : ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < a → IsZero (M.X j))
    (α : M ⟶ I)
    [QuasiIso α] :
    QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op P)).map α)
